subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk be enabled by implicit OpenAI realtime credential availability, or only after an explicit Gateway realtime readiness/preflight says the current Talk setup can start?
rationale: Current code and docs make browser Talk a realtime-provider feature, while this report expects local/non-Realtime Talk configuration not to start OpenAI WebRTC; either answer changes user-facing setup semantics and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Gate On Gateway Readiness
options.body: Use Gateway realtime readiness/preflight to disable or block Talk before microphone/WebRTC startup while preserving whichever credential policy maintainers choose.

options.title: Keep Implicit Credential Activation
options.body: Accept that configured OpenAI realtime credentials enable browser Talk and focus the remaining work on clearer provider/API error messages.

options.title: Require Explicit Realtime Config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when talk.realtime is explicitly configured, with any needed upgrade note or migration for existing users.

recommendation.title: Gate On Gateway Readiness
recommendation.body: Use Gateway realtime readiness/preflight to disable or block Talk before microphone/WebRTC startup while preserving whichever credential policy maintainers choose.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged OpenAI realtime auth and docs work makes this the closest current owner trail for the enablement policy choice.
